groups.name: Kentucky Veterans Program Trust Fund (VPTF)
groups.desc: State trust fund that awards grants to projects and programs serving Kentucky veterans when other funds are not available. Organizations apply through KDVA; funded in part by Kentucky veteran license plate fees and donations.
groups.note: Submit applications to KDVA.PIO@KY.GOV. This is primarily a program/project grant fund, not an individual emergency-assistance program (see also the Kentucky Homeless Veterans Grant Program).

groups.name: Kentucky State Parks — Disabled Veteran Lodging & Military Discounts
groups.desc: Kentucky residents who are 100% disabled as a direct result of a service-connected incident may receive free lodge, cottage, or campsite lodging for up to three visits per calendar year (three nights per visit), subject to availability. The official deals page also lists a military lodging/camping discount and free camping for Kentucky POWs with a VA-issued POW card.
groups.note: Reservations for the 100% disabled-veteran free stay are made by calling the park of choice, no more than 10 days before arrival. Bring the VA disability letter and proof of Kentucky residency. Memorial Day–Labor Day and October stays must start/end Sunday–Thursday. The free accommodation applies only to the room, cottage, or campsite occupied by the veteran.

groups.name: Dependency & Indemnity Compensation (DIC) — Survivors
groups.desc: Tax-exempt monthly benefit for surviving spouses, children, and parents of veterans who died from service-connected causes.

groups.name: VA Aid & Attendance / Housebound Benefits
groups.desc: Additional pension for veterans who need daily personal care assistance or are mostly housebound.

groups.name: VA Disability Compensation
groups.desc: Monthly tax-free payments for veterans with service-connected disabilities. Rating from 0– 100% determines payment amount.
groups.note: VA benefits hotline: 800-827-1000. TTY: 711. An accredited VSO, claims agent, or attorney can help you file at no charge for VSO services.

groups.name: VA Life Insurance Programs (SGLI, VGLI, S-DVI)
groups.desc: Multiple VA life insurance programs for veterans and service members.

groups.name: VA Pension (Non-Service-Connected)
groups.desc: Monthly needs-based pension for wartime veterans with limited income and net worth who are disabled or age 65+.

groups.name: Somerset VA Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) — Nearest to London
groups.desc: Primary care and mental health services. Approximately 45 miles from London, KY. Mon–Fri 8AM–4:30PM.

groups.name: Berea VA Clinic
groups.desc: VA Lexington Health Care System outpatient clinic in Berea offering primary care for Veterans in the region.
groups.note: Hours listed as Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. VA Health Connect: 833-940-1625. TTY: 711.

groups.name: Prestonsburg VA Clinic (Huntington VA Health Care)
groups.desc: Community-based outpatient clinic in the Huntington VA Health Care System offering primary care, mental health, women's health, podiatry, laboratory services, and more for veterans in the Prestonsburg / Floyd County area.
groups.note: Address and main phone confirmed on the official VA Prestonsburg clinic page (JSON-LD). An older public listing at 5230 KY Route 321 is outdated; use the North Highland Avenue address.

groups.name: Hazard VA Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC)
groups.desc: Primary care services for eastern Kentucky veterans, including primary care, mental health, women's health, physical therapy, and telehealth.

groups.name: Lexington VA Health Care System — Franklin R. Sousley Campus
groups.desc: Additional Lexington VA campus providing healthcare services to Kentucky veterans.
groups.note: Main facility hours listed as Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. VA Health Connect: 833-940-1625. TTY: 711.

groups.name: Lexington VA Health Care System — Troy Bowling Campus (Full Medical Center)
groups.desc: Full-service VA Medical Center including inpatient, outpatient, specialty care, surgery, PTSD residential, substance use, and geriatric services.
groups.note: Emergency Department is listed as open 24 hours, 7 days a week. VA Health Connect: 833-940-1625. TTY: 711.

groups.name: Paul E. Patton Eastern Kentucky Veterans Center (Hazard)
groups.desc: 120-bed state veterans nursing home offering long-term care, rehabilitation, memory care, and social services.
groups.note: Administrator listed as Sonya Melton. Admission information is available through KDVA Veterans Centers pages.

groups.name: Thomson-Hood Veterans Center (Nearest State Veterans Nursing Home)
groups.desc: State-operated skilled nursing facility for qualifying veterans: long-term care, memory care, therapy, and social services.

groups.name: Kentucky Veterans Centers — All State Facilities
groups.desc: KY operates multiple skilled long-term care communities: Hazard, Hanson, Radcliff, Florence, and Wilmore.

groups.name: Morehead VA Clinic
groups.desc: Lexington VA Health Care System community-based outpatient clinic offering primary care and related services. Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
groups.address: 333 Beacon Hill Road, Suite 100, Morehead, KY 40351-6182
groups.note: For appointments and after-hours needs you can also use VA Health Connect at 1-833-940-1625 (already listed under Federal healthcare).

groups.name: Carl M. Brashear Radcliff Veterans Center
groups.desc: 120-bed Kentucky state veterans nursing home in Radcliff offering 24/7 skilled nursing care and rehabilitation for eligible Kentucky veterans.
groups.note: Administrator listed on the official KDVA page as Sue Popplewell.

groups.name: Joseph Eddie Ballard Western Kentucky Veterans Center (Hanson)
groups.desc: 156-bed Kentucky state veterans nursing home in Hanson offering long-term skilled nursing care for eligible Kentucky veterans, including a dementia/Alzheimer's wing.
groups.note: The official KDVA facility page confirms the Hanson location but does not publish a local phone or street address. Address and main phone are from the facility's official CMS NPPES / NPI record (NPI 1063784197, last updated February 24, 2025). An activities-director line, (270) 322-3566, is published on the KDVA Activities page.

groups.name: Robert E. Spiller Bowling Green Veterans Center
groups.desc: Kentucky's newest state veterans nursing home — 60 private suites with private baths — providing skilled nursing care for eligible Kentucky veterans in Bowling Green.
groups.note: Admissions inquiries: Deb Gatto, (270) 535-2346, Deb.Gatto@ky.gov, as listed on the official KDVA page. That page still includes older 'anticipated Spring 2026' language; a KDVA ribbon-cutting announced the facility open on September 29, 2026. Confirm current admission status on the official page.

groups.name: Robley Rex VA Medical Center (Louisville)
groups.desc: VA Louisville Health Care System medical center providing primary, specialty, mental health, and hospital care for veterans in Kentucky.

groups.name: VA Caregiver Support Program
groups.desc: Support, education, and financial stipends for family members and friends who serve as caregivers for eligible veterans.
groups.note: Caregiver Support Line hours listed as Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET. TTY: 711. The Veteran generally must be enrolled in VA health care first.

groups.name: VA Community Care Network (Outside VA Network)
groups.desc: When VA cannot provide care, eligible veterans may receive it from community providers at VA expense through the MISSION Act.

groups.name: VA Health Care Enrollment
groups.desc: All veterans should apply for VA health care enrollment, regardless of disability status or income.
groups.note: TTY: 711. You can also apply at VA.gov or at a VA medical facility.

groups.name: VA Substance Use Disorder (SUD) Treatment
groups.desc: VA-covered treatment for alcohol, drugs, and prescription medication misuse.

groups.name: VA Women Veterans Program
groups.desc: Specialized healthcare and services for women veterans including MST counseling, reproductive health, mental health, and benefits assistance.

groups.name: VA Health Connect
groups.desc: Phone line listed on Lexington VA Health Care System clinic pages for health connection and related care questions.
groups.note: TTY: 711. For emergencies, call 911 or use the Troy Bowling Campus Emergency Department.

groups.name: CHAMPVA
groups.desc: Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs — cost-sharing health coverage for eligible spouses, dependents, and survivors of Veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities, and for certain primary family caregivers. Not for people eligible for TRICARE.
groups.address: CHAMPVA, PO Box 500, Spring City, PA 19475
groups.note: Call 1-800-733-8387 (TTY 711), Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–7:30 p.m. ET, or use Ask VA. Apply online or with VA Form 10-10d.

groups.name: TRICARE East (Humana Military)
groups.desc: Department of Defense health care program for active duty, National Guard and Reserve members (when eligible), retirees, and their families. Kentucky is in the TRICARE East Region, administered by Humana Military.
groups.note: Hours listed on the official TRICARE Call Us page as 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. ET and CT, Monday–Friday. Pharmacy: Express Scripts 1-877-363-1303. DEERS eligibility is listed separately under Veteran Identification.

groups.name: Hershel “Woody” Williams VA Medical Center (Huntington, WV)
groups.desc: Regional VA medical center serving eastern Kentucky and neighboring states. The Prestonsburg VA Clinic is part of this health care system.

groups.name: James H. Quillen VA Medical Center (Mountain Home, TN)
groups.desc: VA Mountain Home Health Care System medical center in Johnson City / Mountain Home, Tennessee, serving veterans in Kentucky's southeastern border counties as well as northeast Tennessee.
groups.address: Corner of Lamont Street and Veterans Way, Mountain Home, TN 37684

groups.name: Bell-Whitley Community Action Agency
groups.desc: Community action agency serving Bell and Whitley County residents, including veterans, with housing, utility, and emergency assistance.

groups.name: KCEOC Community Action Partnership
groups.desc: Serves the Cumberland Valley region — Bell, Clay, Harlan, Jackson, Knox, Laurel, Rockcastle & Whitley Counties. Rental/utility assistance, homelessness prevention and rapid rehousing, weatherization, and LIHEAP.
groups.address: 5448 North US Hwy 25E, Suite A, Gray, KY 40734

groups.name: Kentucky River Foothills Development Council — SSVF (Serves Laurel County)
groups.desc: SSVF program covering Laurel County — rental/utility deposits, eviction prevention, emergency rental assistance, and case management.

groups.name: Lake Cumberland Community Action Agency
groups.desc: Serves Adair, Casey, Clinton, Cumberland, Green, McCreary, Pulaski, Russell, Taylor & Wayne Counties with housing, utility, and emergency assistance.

groups.name: Daniel Boone Community Action Agency
groups.desc: Community action agency serving Clay, Jackson, Laurel, Rockcastle, Lee, Owsley, and Wolfe Counties with housing, utility, transit, and emergency assistance that veterans and their families may use.
groups.note: Central office is in Manchester. A Laurel County office is listed at 188 Dog Patch Trading Center, London, KY 40741. Other county offices are listed on the official contact page.

groups.name: LKLP Community Action Council
groups.desc: Community action agency serving Leslie, Knott, Letcher, and Perry Counties with housing, utility, food, and transportation assistance that veterans and their families may use.

groups.name: Veterans Transitional Housing Center (VTHC) — Mountain Comprehensive Care
groups.desc: 25-unit transitional housing program in Pikeville for veterans experiencing homelessness, with supportive services for up to two years, including case management, benefits help, employment readiness, and mental health and substance use counseling.
groups.note: Official Mountain Comprehensive Care Center VTHC page. The program works with the Huntington VA Medical Center. Call before donating items.

groups.name: Kentucky Housing Corporation (KHC) — VETT Program
groups.desc: Veterans Emerging Towards Transition — Housing Choice Vouchers for qualifying homeless veterans in 87 KY counties.

groups.name: Volunteers of America (VOA) Mid-States — SSVF Kentucky
groups.desc: SSVF services promoting housing stability for very low-income veteran families — rental assistance, utility help, case management.

groups.name: Health Care for Homeless Veterans (HCHV) — VA
groups.desc: VA outreach and case management for homeless veterans connecting them to VA healthcare, mental health, and housing services.

groups.name: HUD-VASH (HUD-VA Supportive Housing) Program
groups.desc: Combines HUD Housing Choice Vouchers with VA case management for homeless veterans seeking permanent housing.
groups.note: Ask the Lexington VA Health Care System about local HUD-VASH, or call the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838.

groups.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans — VA
groups.desc: 24/7 hotline connecting homeless or at-risk veterans to emergency shelter, supportive housing, health care, and other resources.

groups.name: VA Home Loan Program
groups.desc: VA-backed home loans with no down payment required, no PMI, and competitive rates for eligible veterans.
groups.note: Apply and learn eligibility on VA.gov. The VA benefits hotline is 800-827-1000.

groups.name: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) Grant
groups.desc: Grants up to $109,986 for severely disabled veterans to build, buy, or modify a home for independent living.

groups.name: VA Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) — National
groups.desc: Rapid re-housing and homelessness prevention including temporary rental assistance, deposits, and utility help for very low-income veteran families.
groups.note: For the local provider serving Laurel County and surrounding counties, see Kentucky River Foothills SSVF. You can also call 877-424-3838.

groups.name: Homes For Our Troops
groups.desc: Builds and donates specially adapted custom homes nationwide for severely injured post-9/11 veterans.

groups.name: Tunnel to Towers Foundation
groups.desc: Provides housing support for catastrophically injured veterans, fallen-first-responder families, and related mortgage-free and adaptive-housing programs.

groups.name: AppalReD Legal Aid — Legal Services for Veterans
groups.desc: Free civil legal aid for low-income residents of eastern and south-central Kentucky, including Laurel, Knox, Whitley, Bell, and Clay Counties through the Barbourville office. The veterans program helps Veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness with issues such as eviction, benefits, family law, and bankruptcy. Low-income Veterans are also served regardless of discharge status.
groups.note: Call Central Intake at 1-866-277-5733 or apply online. Monthly drop-in clinics are held at the Somerset, Hazard, and Berea VA clinics. To pre-register for the Somerset VA clinic, call (606) 802-4188.

groups.name: Kentucky Office of Veteran Legal Services — KDVA
groups.desc: KY state office partnering with legal agencies to provide legal services to veterans across the Commonwealth.

groups.name: Legal Aid of the Bluegrass (Serves Southeastern Kentucky)
groups.desc: Free civil legal services for low-income individuals including veterans in eastern and southeastern Kentucky.

groups.name: Kentucky Legal Aid — Veteran Services
groups.desc: Free civil legal aid for eligible Veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness in western Kentucky (offices in Bowling Green, Madisonville, Paducah, and Owensboro), including housing, family law, income support, and expungement.
groups.note: Southeastern Kentucky veterans should start with AppalReD Legal Aid (already listed under Local). Kentucky Legal Aid's service area is western Kentucky. Bowling Green also: (270) 782-1924.

groups.name: Legal Aid Society — Veterans' Hotline (Louisville)
groups.desc: Free civil legal aid for eligible veterans in the Legal Aid Society service area (Louisville / Jefferson County and surrounding counties served by the Society). Dedicated veterans' hotline.
groups.address: 416 W. Muhammad Ali Boulevard, Suite 300, Louisville, KY
groups.note: Southeastern Kentucky veterans should start with AppalReD Legal Aid (already listed under Local). General Legal Aid Society lines: (502) 584-1254 and 1-800-292-1862.

groups.name: Kentucky Veterans Treatment Court (Specialty Courts)
groups.desc: Veterans Treatment Court dockets overseen by the Kentucky Department of Specialty Courts, offering justice-involved veterans structured treatment, supervision, and case management as an alternative path through the court system. Referrals go through the local court / public defender.
groups.note: Phone and Frankfort address are published on the official Kentucky Court of Justice Specialty Courts page (Administrative Office of the Courts). Ask a local public defender or court about veterans treatment court availability in your county.

groups.name: VA Accredited Claims Agents & Attorneys
groups.desc: Directory of VA-accredited attorneys and claims agents who can represent veterans in claims and appeals.

groups.name: Veterans Club Inc.
groups.desc: Kentucky nonprofit offering connection, healing and recovery programs, housing assistance, and vocational training for veterans and first responders, including equine-assisted and community events.
groups.note: Address and phone confirmed on the official Veterans Club Inc. contact page.

groups.name: American Red Cross Military & Veteran Caregiver Network
groups.desc: Emergency communication, financial assistance, counseling referrals, and support for active duty, veterans, and families.

groups.name: Canine Companions for Independence (Service Dogs for Veterans)
groups.desc: Provides highly trained assistance dogs for veterans with disabilities at no cost.
groups.address: North Central Training Center serves Kentucky

groups.name: Fisher House Foundation
groups.desc: Free lodging for military and veteran families near VA hospitals while loved ones receive treatment.

groups.name: Folds of Honor
groups.desc: Educational scholarships for spouses and children of fallen or disabled service members and first responders.

groups.name: Gary Sinise Foundation
groups.desc: Programs supporting severely wounded warriors, building smart homes for disabled veterans, and supporting first responders.

groups.name: Iraq & Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA)
groups.desc: Advocacy and services for post-9/11 veterans including mental health, benefits navigation, and community connection.

groups.name: Kentucky Wounded Heroes
groups.desc: Kentucky nonprofit providing outdoor healing activities (hunting, fishing, travel) to honor and support the emotional wellness of wounded veterans, first responders, and EMS.

groups.name: Military Order of the Purple Heart
groups.desc: Represents combat-wounded veterans in VA claims and provides service programs.

groups.name: Mission Continues
groups.desc: Connects veterans with volunteer service platoons, giving veterans a continued sense of purpose and community.

groups.name: National Veterans Foundation
groups.desc: Crisis intervention, case management, and direct services for veterans in need via a 24/7 tollfree helpline.

groups.name: Operation Homefront
groups.desc: Financial assistance, transitional housing, and long-term stability programs for military families including emergency relief.

groups.name: Paralyzed Veterans of America (PVA) — National
groups.desc: Benefits advocacy and resources specifically for veterans with spinal cord injury or disease.

groups.name: Semper Fi & America's Fund
groups.desc: Financial assistance and lifetime support for combat-wounded, critically ill, and catastrophically injured service members, veterans, and their families.

groups.name: Team Red White & Blue (Team RWB)
groups.desc: Physical and social activity programs connecting veterans to community. Chapters across Kentucky.

groups.name: Team Rubicon
groups.desc: Unites the skills and experience of military veterans with first responders to rapidly deploy disaster response teams.

groups.name: Wounded Warrior Project (WWP)
groups.desc: Programs supporting post-9/11 injured veterans: mental health, career counseling, peer support, physical wellness, and family support.

groups.name: Hope For The Warriors
groups.desc: National nonprofit providing critical needs assistance, career and educational programs, and support for post-9/11 service members, veterans, and military families.
groups.note: Main line: 877-2HOPE4W (877-246-7349). A National Women Veterans Hotline is listed separately under Women Veterans Resources.

groups.name: K9s For Warriors
groups.desc: Provides trained service dogs at no cost to veterans and service members with PTSD, traumatic brain injury, or military sexual trauma.
groups.address: 114 Camp K9 Road, Ponte Vedra, FL 32081
groups.note: Official contact page also lists a local line, (904) 686-1956.

groups.name: Student Veterans of America (SVA)
groups.desc: National network of student-veteran campus chapters offering community, advocacy, and support for veterans in higher education.

groups.name: SAMHSA Veterans Mental Health & Substance Use Resources
groups.desc: National treatment referral, information, and support services for veterans struggling with substance use and mental health issues.

groups.name: VA Substance Use Disorder (SUD) Treatment Locator
groups.desc: VA provides residential, intensive outpatient, and outpatient SUD treatment for alcohol, opioids, and other substances.

groups.name: KDVA Transportation for Veterans — Medical/Behavioral Health
groups.desc: Kentucky state program providing transportation assistance for veterans to reach medical and behavioral health appointments.

groups.name: DAV Transportation Network — Free Rides to VA Appointments
groups.desc: DAV coordinates volunteer drivers to provide free transportation for veterans who have no other way to get to their VA medical appointments.

groups.name: VA Beneficiary Travel (Mileage Reimbursement)
groups.desc: VA reimburses eligible veterans for travel costs to VA appointments.

groups.name: Kentucky Veteran Designation on Driver's License
groups.desc: Veterans can have a 'VETERAN' designation added to their KY driver's license or ID card as proof of service.
groups.address: Apply at any KY Circuit Court Clerk / DMV Office

groups.address: National Personnel Records Center, 1 Archives Dr, St. Louis, MO 63138

groups.desc: Official VA-issued photo ID for veterans with honorable discharge. Free and accepted as proof of service at many businesses for discounts.

groups.name: KDVA Women Veterans Programs
groups.desc: Kentucky state programs and outreach specifically addressing the unique needs of women veterans.

groups.name: Lady Veterans Connect — Thurman-Abbott House

groups.note: Contacts confirmed on the official Lady Veterans Connect contact page.

groups.name: VA Military Sexual Trauma (MST) Counseling

groups.name: VA Women Veterans Call Center
groups.desc: Dedicated line for women veterans to ask questions about VA benefits, health care, Military Sexual Trauma (MST), and services.

groups.name: Hope For The Warriors — National Women Veterans Hotline

groups.note: Published on the official Hope For The Warriors contact page as the National Women Veterans Hotline.

groups.name: United Way of Laurel County / 211 Helpline

groups.name: Come-Unity Cooperative Care (London)
groups.desc: Local community assistance organization in London providing food and related emergency help for Laurel County residents, including veterans and their families.
groups.note: Address, phone, and hours (Tuesday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; Saturday 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.) published in the Laurel County Health Department official food pantry guide.

groups.name: God's Pantry Food Bank — London
groups.desc: Regional food bank serving southeastern Kentucky, with a London site listed by the Laurel County Health Department for food assistance.
groups.note: London address, phone, and hours (Monday–Friday 7:00 a.m.–3:30 p.m.) published in the Laurel County Health Department official food pantry guide. The food bank's own contact page lists its Lexington headquarters at 2201 Innovation Drive, Lexington, KY 40511, (859) 255-6592, info@godspantry.org.

groups.name: Good Samaritan House (London)
groups.desc: Local soup kitchen and community assistance in downtown London serving residents in need, including veterans and their families.
groups.note: Address, phone, and soup kitchen hours (11:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.) published in the Laurel County Health Department official food pantry guide.

groups.name: Helping Hands Food Pantry (Corbin)
groups.desc: Local food pantry in the Corbin area serving residents in need, including veterans and their families.
groups.note: Address, phone, and hours (Monday and Thursday 10:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.) published in the Laurel County Health Department official food pantry guide.

groups.name: Laurel County Health Department
groups.desc: Local health department providing public health services and maintaining a community resource guide (including food pantries) used by Laurel County residents, including veterans and their families.
groups.note: Official site also lists (606) 878-7754. Hours: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
